passage:
When I moved from Shillong to Bengaluru for college, everything was new at once: the language on the buses, the food, the noise, the fact that nobody noticed if I slept till noon. By October I was eating biscuits for dinner at midnight and crying on the phone to Mom.
So I built a few anchors. One wake time, seven, even on Sundays. A walk round the lake near the hostel every morning before class. Meals in the mess at the same times, even on busy days. And the Thursday choir, where Yusuf, a second-year, saved me a seat in the first week.
None of it was exciting. But when an exam went badly or I missed home, the anchors held. I'm Ira, and I still walk that lake.

qa.q: What does Ira join on Thursdays?
qa.a: Ira joins the Thursday choir.

qa.q: How did Ira feel by October?
qa.a: Ira felt lonely and unsettled, eating biscuits at midnight and crying on the phone to Mom.

qa.q: Which anchors did Ira build, and how did they help?
qa.a: A set wake time, a morning lake walk, regular mess meals and the choir, which held Ira steady when an exam went badly or home felt far away.

qa.q: How might Yusuf have seen the new first-year?
qa.a: Yusuf seemed to see someone new who could use a welcome, and so saved a seat in the very first week.

grounding: A young adult living away from home steadies mood with anchors: a set wake time, a morning walk, regular meals and one fixed social activity.

passage:
Mentor's log, first-year hostel, Pune. Santosh Hegde.
Chinmay has missed three morning labs this fortnight. His roommate says he sleeps at four, skips the mess and plays games online till dawn. When I met him today he looked grey and admitted, "Half the time I don't know what day it is. At home Aai did everything."
We made a small plan together, with Chinmay choosing each part: an alarm at seven every day, breakfast in the mess before lab, a walk to the gate and back, and one fixed thing each week to look forward to. He picked the Saturday football match.
I'll check in next week. He shook my hand as he left, a little embarrassed but lighter.

qa.q: How many morning labs had Chinmay missed?
qa.a: Chinmay missed three morning labs this fortnight.

qa.q: How did Chinmay feel admitting he didn't know what day it was?
qa.a: Chinmay felt lost and a little embarrassed, missing the structure Aai used to give.

qa.q: Why was it wise to let Chinmay choose each part of the plan?
qa.a: Anchors Chinmay picks himself, like the seven o'clock alarm and Saturday football, are more likely to stick than rules handed down.

qa.q: How might Chinmay's roommate have been affected by the late nights?
qa.a: The roommate may have been disturbed by the gaming till dawn and worried enough to mention it.

grounding: A young adult away from home is steadied by anchors: a set wake time, regular meals, a short walk and one fixed social activity.

passage:
Thursday
Six weeks into college in Pune, far from home, and today I felt steady for the first time. Wrote down why, so I don't forget.
The first month was chaos. Slept at random, skipped the mess, lay in bed missing everyone. So I've built a few anchors. Alarm at seven, every day, even Sunday. Walk to the tea stall by the gate before class. Breakfast, lunch and dinner at the mess at the proper times, even when I'm not that hungry. And Wednesday football with Pranav and the others from my floor, which I never skip. It sounds boring written down. But when the rest of life is brand new, these things stay the same, and that helps. Pranav said I look less lost.
Gurpreet

qa.q: What time is Gurpreet's alarm?
qa.a: At seven.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel during the first month at college?
qa.a: Gurpreet felt lost and homesick, missing everyone amid the chaos.

qa.q: Which anchors has Gurpreet built?
qa.a: A seven o'clock alarm, a walk to the tea stall, regular mess meals and Wednesday football with Pranav.

qa.q: How has Pranav noticed the change?
qa.a: Pranav said Gurpreet looks less lost now.

grounding: Shows a young adult away from home building anchors of wake time, a morning walk, regular meals and one fixed social activity that steady mood.

Bhavna: how's the big city? you've been quiet
Farida: honestly the first month was awful. new job, new flat, nobody to talk to. I was sleeping at weird times and eating chips for dinner
Bhavna: oh Farida 😔
Farida: but it's getting better. I made some rules for myself
Bhavna: rules?
Farida: up at 6:30 every day. walk round the lake before work. lunch at 1 and dinner at 8, like at home
Farida: and Saturday morning I joined a pottery class. same people every week
Bhavna: that sounds so like Ammi's routine
Farida: haha I know. but when everything is new, having a few things the same makes me feel less adrift
Bhavna: proud of you. call on Sunday?
Farida: always

qa.q: What class did Farida join on Saturday mornings?
qa.a: A pottery class.

qa.q: How did Farida feel during the first month in the city?
qa.a: Farida felt lonely and adrift, sleeping at odd times and eating chips for dinner.

qa.q: Why do Farida's small rules help?
qa.a: Regular wake-up, walks, meals and a weekly class give fixed points when everything else is new.

qa.q: How might Bhavna feel reading about Farida's rules?
qa.a: Bhavna is likely to feel relieved and proud, since the rules sound like their mother's routine.

grounding: Shows a young adult living away from home building anchors of wake time, a walk, regular meals and one fixed social activity to steady mood.

passage: When Nilesh moved from Nagpur to a small town near Wardha for his agriculture diploma, nothing was the same. The room above the grocery shop was noisy, the food was different, and he knew no one. For two weeks he slept late, skipped breakfast and spent evenings on his phone, feeling low. Then he made a plan. He set his alarm for six-thirty and walked to the river before class, watching the fishermen push off. He ate at the dhaba at the same times every day, so the owner started keeping his roti hot. And on Sundays he joined the bhajan group at the temple, where he met Ira, a classmate who sang loudly and badly. By the end of the month the town felt less strange, and so did he.

qa.q: Where did Nilesh walk before class?
qa.a: To the river.

qa.q: How did Nilesh feel during the first two weeks?
qa.a: He felt low and lonely, knowing no one in a strange town.

qa.q: Which anchors helped Nilesh settle?
qa.a: A fixed wake-up time, a morning walk to the river, meals at the same times and Sunday bhajans.

qa.q: How might the dhaba owner have seen Nilesh?
qa.a: The owner probably saw a regular young customer and grew fond enough to keep his roti hot.

grounding: Shows a young adult away from home building anchors of wake time, a walk, regular meals and a weekly social activity that steady mood.

passage: Beatriz's first month in Rotterdam was a blur of new streets, a shared kitchen that smelled of other people's dinners, and lectures in a second language. She slept at three, woke at noon and felt jittery by evening. In October she wrote four lines on a sticky note above her desk: up at 7:30. Walk along the canal. Lunch at one, dinner at seven. Saturday football. The canal walk was cold and grey, but her head felt clearer after it. On Saturdays Chidi, a midfielder from her floor, started saving her a seat on the tram. By November the city was still strange, but her days had a shape, and she caught herself humming while chopping onions.

qa.q: What did Beatriz write on the sticky note above her desk?
qa.a: Up at 7:30, a walk along the canal, lunch at one and dinner at seven, and Saturday football.

qa.q: How was Beatriz feeling in her first month, and what shows it?
qa.a: She felt unsettled and jittery; she slept at three, woke at noon and was on edge by evening.

qa.q: Why did these small anchors help when everything else was new?
qa.a: They gave her days a predictable shape with regular daylight, meals and company, which steadied her mood.

qa.q: What might Chidi notice about Beatriz on Saturdays by November?
qa.a: Chidi would probably see a steadier, friendlier teammate who turns up on time, and might enjoy the regular company too.

grounding: Shows a young adult living away from home steadying her mood with a regular wake time, a morning walk, set meal times and one fixed social activity.
